name: bringup-d1-vap
about: Bring-up matrix row vap (D1): the cfg80211 netdev VAP lifecycle through the driver + nl80211 (M0/M1) - wiphy registration gate, iw phy enumeration, iw interface add, netdev sysfs checks, iw dev del, and the cfg80211_status VAP counters before/after. No H2D message is fired: M1 is the driver's own netdev model.

steps.name: cfg-status
steps.about: the wiphy registration gate fired after the ready handshake: allocated + registered, no VAP yet

steps.name: phy-info
steps.about: iw phy phy0 info enumerates the clean wiphy (read-only)

steps.name: vap-add
steps.about: M1: iw phy phy0 interface add wlan0 type managed -> real netdev through add_virtual_intf

steps.name: netdev-type
steps.about: the netdev exists and is ARPHRD_ETHER (sysfs type=1)

steps.name: netdev-addr
steps.about: the netdev carries a locally-administered style address (the 2026-11-25 milestone saw 02:00:68:69:35:01)

steps.name: vap-added
steps.about: the driver model recorded the VAP: vap0 line + netdev created counter

steps.name: dev-list
steps.about: iw dev lists the new interface

steps.name: vap-del
steps.about: M1 teardown: iw dev wlan0 del -> del_virtual_intf unregisters the wdev/netdev

steps.name: vap-removed
steps.about: the VAP model is empty again: vaps=0 and the netdev removed counter

steps.name: dev-list-after
steps.about: iw dev no longer lists wlan0

steps.name: note-end
steps.about: D1 row PASS = wiphy registered + netdev add/del both round-trip; a failure is a driver-model bug, not a firmware event (no H2D was sent). NOTE: the firmware VAP/user messages (g0 id7/id8 user_add, g0 id9 del_user) are the wifi-vap-scan lane's byte-exact builders (recipes/frames.md) and need a driver provider registration; this row deliberately stops at the hardware-validated M1 netdev model.
